title: Cohort-based Roadmap Runway for Private Instance Upgrade Windows
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Problem: Enterprise customers operating Private/VPC/on-prem instances require predictable upgrade windows, compatibility guarantees, and a clear runway for activation. Currently, our roadmap has one-off rollouts that create uneven capacity demand, surprise regressions, and long sales cycles for tenants who need strict maintenance windows. This ticket defines a cohort-based quarterly runway (activation windows + compatibility gates) to plan and communicate Private upgrade waves tied to OKRs.

Goal: Create a repeatable plan for rolling private deployments through ordered cohorts per quarter, with clear compatibility gates, engineering readiness signals, and a customer communications playbook. This should reduce upgrade friction, shorten time-to-activation, and enable revenue-recognizable activations in the quarter.

Scope:
- Define cohort sizing and prioritization criteria (security-critical, purchased contracts, high-usage tenants).
- Establish compatibility verification steps (schema, API stability, networking, KMS/HSM integrations).
- Map capacity and Dedicated pool hedges required for each wave.
- Produce runbook templates (customer comms, rollback criteria, SRE on-call play).
- Align OKRs and tracking metrics for the quarter across PM, Eng, Sales, and Support.

Out of scope: automated in-place upgrades for air-gapped on-prem packages and full self-service onboarding (handled by separate initiative).
acceptance_criteria: Written cohort prioritization framework published in Confluence and reviewed by GTM and SRE
Compatibility verifier checklist with automated smoke tests and manual gating steps exists
Runbook templates (pre-upgrade checklist, rollback playbook, customer comms) available and validated with two pilot customers
Capacity hedging plan documented with Dedicated team and signed off by Eng infra lead
Quarter OKRs updated to include activation rate target and time-to-activation SLAs
tasks: Draft prioritization rubric and sample cohort list (PM)
Build compatibility verifier checklist and run initial automation (Eng)
Create customer comms templates and legal check for maintenance windows (GTM/Legal)
Coordinate Dedicated capacity reservations for projected waves (Infra ops)
Run pilot upgrade with 2 customers and capture learnings (Solutions Eng)
Finalize acceptance criteria and publish playbooks to internal Confluence
risks: High variability in customer readiness causing wave slippage
Hidden integration regressions for KMS/HSM configurations
Insufficient Dedicated capacity during overlapping customer windows
Sales commitments misaligned with actual engineering delivery dates
decisions: Cohorts will be sized by 'activation units' (monthly token baseline + integration complexity) rather than headcount
We will require a green smoke test and a documented manual signoff from the customer before marking activation complete
Compatibility verifier will initially focus on API/Model contract, networking, and KMS; filesystem and custom plugins are deferred
metrics: Activation rate (% of targeted cohort activated within window)
Mean time-to-activation (days from kick-off to green smoke test)
Fraction of upgrades requiring manual engineering intervention
